beats.label: S1 · The pitch
beats.text: Félix, a Sinaloa cop, moves to Guadalajara and pitches unifying every regional trafficker under one federation — peace and shared routes in exchange for tax.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Establishes the federation model whose collapse in S2 defines the entire series.

beats.label: S1 · A cartel is born
beats.text: Rafa proves a seedless-marijuana empire is possible in the desert. When holdout boss Avilés is killed by police, Félix takes the head of a unified Guadalajara cartel.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Introduces Rafa and puts Félix at the top — the position everything in S2 revolves around.

beats.label: S1 · Kiki hits a wall
beats.text: New DEA agent Kiki Camarena discovers the corruption reaches from local cops up to the DFS; every raid he plans is tipped off before he arrives.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Sets up why Kiki must go rogue, which triggers his murder and Operation Leyenda in S2.

beats.label: S1 · Enter the Colombians
beats.text: Félix opens a cocaine pipeline for the Colombians and becomes their key transporter. Kiki's US sting to arrest him is blown by a political tip-off from Mexico City.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The Cali relationship and political protection are the two levers Félix wields throughout S2.

beats.label: S1 · Kiki kidnapped
beats.text: A DEA-led raid burns Rafa's massive marijuana crop. Azul persuades a paranoid Rafa to kidnap Kiki, who is interrogated and tortured over days at a Guadalajara ranch.
beats.whyLoadBearing: This is the crime Walt Breslin spends all of S2 avenging, one link in the chain at a time.

beats.label: S1 · The betrayal
beats.text: Kiki's body is found. Félix anonymously gives up Rafa and lets Don Neto be arrested, sacrificing his partners to save the empire and keep his political protection.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Explains why Félix enters S2 alone at the top and why nobody around him fully trusts him.

beats.label: S1 · Leyenda begins
beats.text: Félix crashes a plaza meeting in Ensenada with a new political deal and retakes leadership, kicking Isabella out. The DEA launches Operation Leyenda to hunt Kiki's killers.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Names the DEA operation that structures S2 and shows Isabella cut loose to pursue her own plans.

cliffhanger.text: Félix stands atop a federation he holds together by murder, betrayal and political favours. The DEA has abandoned legal channels and launched Operation Leyenda specifically to bring down everyone who touched Kiki.
questions: How far outside the law will the DEA go once official arrests have all failed?
Can Félix hold the plazas together with Don Neto jailed and Rafa in a cell?
Which of the men Félix has sacrificed or humiliated will move against him first?

characters.name: Miguel Ángel Félix Gallardo
characters.line: Founder and sole head of the Guadalajara Cartel, protected by Mexican politicians after selling out his own partners to save himself.

characters.name: Kiki Camarena
characters.line: DEA agent tortured and killed by Rafa on Félix's watch; the death now drives US retaliation against the cartel.

characters.name: Rafael 'Rafa' Caro Quintero
characters.line: Cocaine-addled marijuana genius, arrested after ordering Kiki's kidnapping when Félix anonymously gave him up.

characters.name: Ernesto 'Don Neto' Fonseca
characters.line: Senior partner arrested at the coast, now aware Félix betrayed him to save the empire.

characters.name: Juan José 'Azul' Esparragoza
characters.line: Félix's quiet strategist, who both pushed Rafa to grab Kiki and warned Félix in time to escape the raid.

characters.name: Isabella Bautista
characters.line: Longtime associate publicly kicked out of the federation at Ensenada; already scheming to source her own Colombian cocaine.

characters.name: The Arellano Félix brothers (Benjamín & Ramón)
characters.line: Volatile Tijuana plaza bosses within the federation, close to Isabella and quick to answer any slight with violence.

characters.name: Joaquín 'El Chapo' Guzmán
characters.line: Sinaloan lieutenant who helped Rafa escape the marijuana raid; still a mid-level figure, not yet a boss.

characters.name: Amado Carrillo Fuentes
characters.line: Rising trafficker attached to the Juárez plaza, briefly glimpsed at the club shooting that put Rafa in DEA sights.

beats.label: S2 · Leyenda goes dark
beats.text: DEA agent Walt Breslin launches Operation Leyenda, kidnapping and torturing the men responsible for Kiki's murder to work his way up the chain toward Félix.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Introduces Walt and the off-the-books methodology that shapes every DEA move for the rest of the series.

beats.label: S2 · The monopoly bet
beats.text: Félix bets his federation on a cocaine monopoly — a deal with Cali to move 70 tons through Amado's Juárez airstrips, freezing out the rival Gulf Cartel.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The 70-ton deal is the spine of S2; Amado's airstrips are the reason Juárez becomes an empire in S3.

beats.label: S2 · The case dies
beats.text: Leyenda catches Zuno, who names Félix on tape but recants at the grand jury. The official investigation is dead, so Walt's team pivots to targeting the trafficking itself.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Explains why the DEA's fight against Félix moves from courts to sabotage — the mode Walt uses through S3.

beats.label: S2 · Plazas turn
beats.text: Plazas turn on each other. El Chapo builds a Sinaloa tunnel under Tijuana; Walt tips the Arellanos, who destroy it and later execute Sinaloan boss Cochiloco in retaliation.
beats.whyLoadBearing: First open blood between Sinaloa and Tijuana — the exact feud that consumes S3.

beats.label: S2 · Rigging the election
beats.text: Félix rigs the 1988 PRI presidential election by crashing the vote-count system, buying himself government protection just as his own plazas begin turning against him.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Shows Félix at maximum political leverage — the peak from which he is deliberately dropped at season's end.

beats.label: S2 · The ambush fails
beats.text: Walt ambushes the 70-ton shipment in Juárez but finds only decoy powder — Amado spotted the trackers and moved the real load. Most of Walt's team is killed and Walt is reassigned.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Establishes Amado's operational cunning and forces Walt into the reassignment he returns from in S3.

beats.label: S2 · The federation breaks
beats.text: Félix murders Palma's family as a warning; the plazas walk out and form the Tijuana, Sinaloa and Juárez cartels. Mexico arrests Félix as a signal to America ahead of NAFTA.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The founding moment of the three cartels whose war IS Season 3.

cliffhanger.text: Félix sits in a Mexican prison, handed to the Americans as a NAFTA offering. From behind bars he warns Walt that the newly independent Tijuana, Sinaloa and Juárez cartels are about to tear the country apart.
questions: Will Amado turn his Juárez airstrips into the successor to Félix's empire?
Can El Chapo and Sinaloa survive the Arellanos' vendetta over the tunnel and the murdered Cochiloco?
Which of the three cartels will Cali choose as its main pipeline into America?

characters.name: Miguel Ángel Félix Gallardo
characters.line: Imprisoned at last, handed over by the Mexican state; still the man who designed the coming war.

characters.name: Walt Breslin
characters.line: DEA agent who ran Operation Leyenda off the books; reassigned after his 70-ton ambush turned to slaughter.

characters.name: Amado Carrillo Fuentes
characters.line: Head of the new Juárez Cartel, controlling the airstrips and the direct line to Cali he built under Félix.

characters.name: The Arellano Félix family (Benjamín, Ramón, Enedina)
characters.line: Ruling family of the new Tijuana Cartel — Benjamín the boss, Ramón the enforcer, Enedina the strategist.

characters.name: Joaquín 'El Chapo' Guzmán
characters.line: Rising Sinaloa Cartel figure whose tunnel triggered the war with Tijuana and left him a marked man.

characters.name: Héctor 'El Güero' Palma
characters.line: Sinaloa boss whose wife was beheaded and children thrown off a bridge by Félix as a warning to the plazas.

characters.name: Juan José 'Azul' Esparragoza
characters.line: Now a founding boss of the Sinaloa Cartel alongside Chapo and Palma.

beats.label: S3 · Amado reinvents Juárez
beats.text: After his daughter's death, Amado rebuilds Juárez as a cell-based operation, executes his liability Aguilar, and partners with billionaire Carlos Hank Gonzalez to launder money.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Sets Amado up as the smartest operator of the season and introduces Hank as the money power behind him.

beats.label: S3 · Blood at the wedding
beats.text: The Arellanos squeeze the Sinaloans with taxes and denied borders. El Chapo answers with an assault on Benjamín's birthday party that kills Enedina's new husband Claudio.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Explains why the AFO's response for the rest of the season is personal, driven by Enedina's grief.

beats.label: S3 · The cardinal at the airport
beats.text: Ramón hunts El Chapo to Guadalajara airport; the shootout kills a Catholic cardinal by mistake. Mexico forms an army task force under General Rebollo to end the drug war.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The event that puts Rebollo and Walt into the story as the state's response to the cartel war.

beats.label: S3 · The other war
beats.text: Walt joins Rebollo's task force. Tijuana journalist Andrea uncovers the narcojuniors and money-laundering ties running from the Arellanos through Hank into the ruling PRI.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Establishes the journalist thread and the political corruption that constrains what any task force can do.

beats.label: S3 · Amado buys the general
beats.text: Cali collapses. Amado becomes the dominant cocaine transporter into America and secretly pays General Rebollo — buying the man leading Mexico's own drug war.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The turning point that makes Amado untouchable and reveals the task force itself is corrupted.

beats.label: S3 · Enedina takes the AFO
beats.text: Enedina takes over the AFO after Benjamín flees and Francisco is arrested, killing Azul. Mayo and El Chapo ally against Tijuana with Amado's money bankrolling the war.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Puts Enedina in charge of the Arellano organisation and shows Mayo emerging as Sinaloa's street power.

beats.label: S3 · Amado vanishes
beats.text: Hank freezes Amado's accounts to force him to end the bloodshed. Amado stages his death during plastic surgery, executes the surgeons, and is last glimpsed alive in Chile.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The season's central mystery — whether Amado is truly gone — and the reason Mexico's cocaine map is now open.

cliffhanger.text: Amado has apparently died in surgery and been buried, but a final shot in Chile shows him alive with his lover, two wine glasses waiting. The Tijuana–Sinaloa war has burned itself down to Enedina holding a shattered AFO and Mayo executing Ramón in the street.
questions: Is Amado's exit real, or will he be pulled back to reclaim what he built?
Can Enedina keep the AFO alive with Benjamín in hiding and Ramón dead?
Will El Chapo run the Sinaloa Cartel from inside his prison cell, or find a way out?

characters.name: Amado Carrillo Fuentes
characters.line: Kingpin who bought General Rebollo, dominated the cocaine trade, then staged his own death and slipped away to Chile.

characters.name: Joaquín 'El Chapo' Guzmán
characters.line: Running the Sinaloa Cartel from inside prison, now the senior figure with Palma finally caught.

characters.name: Ismael 'Mayo' Zambada
characters.line: Sinaloa's street boss who ordered Ramón killed; the most powerful cartel figure not in a cell.

characters.name: Enedina Arellano Félix
characters.line: New head of the AFO after Benjamín's flight, ruling by grief and vengeance since Claudio's murder.

characters.name: Benjamín Arellano Félix
characters.line: Former AFO boss now in hiding after the task force nearly caught him and his family was detained.

characters.name: Ramón Arellano Félix
characters.line: Killed by Mayo's men after Enedina sent him on a mission; the AFO's enforcer is gone.

characters.name: Walt Breslin
characters.line: Back in Mexico with Rebollo's task force, having lost another operation and another informant in Alex.

characters.name: General Jesús Gutiérrez Rebollo
characters.line: Commander of Mexico's drug-war task force and secretly on Amado's payroll.

characters.name: Carlos Hank Gonzalez
characters.line: Billionaire launderer for Amado and the AFO who froze Amado's accounts to force an end to the bloodshed.

characters.name: Andrea Núñez
characters.line: Tijuana journalist at La Voz who exposed the money laundering chain from the AFO through Hank into the PRI.
